title: Gyrotropy from extrinsic geometry in twisted materials
summary: Two-dimensional moiré materials feature widely tunable electronic structures. When these materials are illuminated by light, they exhibit optical gyrotropy in the form of circular dichroism and birefringence. Here, the authors show that this gyrotropy naturally decomposes into an intrinsic contribution due to interlayer electronic coupling and an extrinsic contribution due to the twisted embedding of the material in physical space. The authors conduct a general symmetry analysis applicable to moiré materials and identify regimes in which the intrinsic, and in which the extrinsic contributions dominate the gyrotropy. Finally, they apply the analysis to twisted bilayer graphene and twisted MoTe .
